exposure: Maternal metabolic milieu (glucose, insulin, triglycerides, free fatty acids, TNF-a, high-density lipoprotein, total cholesterol)
Maternal obesity status (obesity vs. normal weight)
outcome: Child adiposity (at birth, 4-6 months, and 4-6 years)
Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) lipid metabolism (lipidomics, TAG stores, acylcarnitines)
cohort: The study included mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) cultured from term infants born to mothers with obesity (n=16) or normal weight (n=15).
finding: MSC phenotypes are predicted by comprehensive maternal metabolic milieu exposures, independent of maternal BMI, and show potential utility as an at-birth predictor for child adiposity at 4-6 years.
